name: cern-ndiff
why: A numerical diff tool from CERN's MAD project, comparing floating-point output for physics work; a rare scientific-software find.

brief.what_it_is: A command-line tool named ndiff, packaged for Homebrew as cern-ndiff with the description "Numerical diff tool". Per the Homebrew formula it installs a single executable, ndiff. From the formula description alone, it compares numerical output files, which is the job a numerical diff does. I could not read its documentation, so I cannot confirm its inputs, tolerance options, or output format.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage I reached did not describe the problem ndiff solves, so I have no author framing. The scout note says it comes from CERN's MAD project and is used to compare floating-point output in physics work, but I could not verify that from the pages I read.
brief.install_notes: Installed through Homebrew as cern-ndiff. The formula lists no caveats. I found no README, so I have no information on runtimes, configuration, or first-run steps beyond the brew install itself.
brief.standout: Unverified. The scout note calls it a rare scientific-software find. A diff tool that tolerates floating-point differences rather than requiring exact text matches would be useful for numerical regression testing, but I could not confirm that this is what ndiff does.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage https://mad.web.cern.ch/mad/ returned only a redirect page with a link to MAD-X and no release or commit information. I found no repository and no release dates.
brief.caveats: The homepage was effectively unreachable for this purpose: it returned only a redirect stub that points to MAD-X rather than ndiff, and the guessed GitHub repository returned 404. Everything about ndiff's behaviour beyond the Homebrew formula description is unverified. The scout note's claims about physics use and CERN origin are unconfirmed.
